items.title: MBDA Offers SM39 Block 2 Mod 2 for Indonesia’s Scorpène Submarines
items.originalTitle: MBDA Offers SM39 Block 2 Mod 2 for Indonesia’s Scorpène Submarines
items.summary: During the ongoing EURONAVAL 2026 Press Tour organised by the French Maritime Industry Association (GICAN), MBDA confirmed that the company is offering its submarine-launched Exocet anti-ship missile for Indonesia’s future Scorpène Evolved submarines. Responding to a question from Naval News , MBDA said it is offering the SM39 Block 2 Mod 2, the latest submarine-launched Exocet variant currently in full production. The company also confirmed that the ongoing contract for two Scorpène Evolved submarines already includes the capability to launch the SM39, as Naval News previously reported .

evidenceRecords.text: During the ongoing EURONAVAL 2026 Press Tour organised by the French Maritime Industry Association (GICAN), MBDA confirmed that the company is offering its submarine-launched Exocet anti-ship missile for Indonesia’s future Scorpène Evolved submarines.
Responding to a question from Naval News , MBDA said it is offering the SM39 Block 2 Mod 2, the latest submarine-launched Exocet variant currently in full production.
The company also confirmed that the ongoing contract for two Scorpène Evolved submarines already includes the capability to launch the SM39, as Naval News previously reported .
MBDA said it is offering the SM39 rather than the next-generation SM40 , which remains under development, because of Indonesia’s submarine production timeline.

The first and second Indonesian Scorpène Evolved submarines are scheduled for delivery in 2032 and 2033 , respectively, and MBDA wants to ensure that the Indonesian Navy (TNI AL) can equip the boats with a submarine-launched anti-ship missile at or soon after delivery if required.
The company said only minimal adjustments would be needed to use the newer missile, as the SM39 and SM40 use the same storage and launch capsule and both fit standard 533 mm submarine torpedo tubes.
MBDA expects Indonesia to formally order SM39 in early 2027.
Submarine Launched Exocet SM39.

About the SM39 Block 2 Mod 2 The SM39 launches from a torpedo tube inside a watertight capsule that carries the missile to the surface before releasing it for low-altitude, sea-skimming, high-subsonic flight.

The Block 2 Mod 2 represents the latest production standard of the SM39, incorporating updated electronics, improved seeker performance, and better electronic counter-countermeasure capability than earlier versions.

items.title: NASA Testing Aims at Supercooled Large Droplet Aviation Safety
items.originalTitle: NASA Testing Aims at Supercooled Large Droplet Aviation Safety
items.summary: NASA is leveraging its expertise and enhancing its test facilities to help address a rare but persistent aviation hazard: icing that occurs when aircraft encounter unusually large, very cold water droplets in clouds. The problem, known as “supercooled large droplet icing,” occurs when aircraft fly through clouds containing unusually large drops of water that are very cold but remain liquid. When a plane passes through those drops, they can rapidly freeze to surfaces that are not protected from ice buildup. The aviation industry relies on engineering tools to help design their aircraft.

items.title: Has the Pentagon given up on AI polygraph analysis of trustworthiness?
items.originalTitle: Has the Pentagon given up on AI polygraph analysis of trustworthiness?
items.summary: As of July, the Pentagon had been prepping artificial intelligence tools that analyze text, voices and faces to estimate trustworthiness, according to declassified presentation slides and prior Defense Department statements. Now, Pentagon officials say that some of that AI is not part of the current revamp of the polygraph interview process, after Defense News asked for a response to concerns about the earlier statements and the slides.

evidenceRecords.text: As of July, the Pentagon had been prepping artificial intelligence tools that analyze text, voices and faces to estimate trustworthiness, according to declassified presentation slides and prior Defense Department statements.

Now, Pentagon officials say that some of that AI is not part of the current revamp of the polygraph interview process, after Defense News asked for a response to concerns about the earlier statements and the slides.

On Wednesday, the Pentagon’s Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency, or DCSA, which vets security clearance holders and applicants, said in an emailed statement that “active research and development” for the “Modernizing Polygraph” effort “does not incorporate generative super intelligence , also known as artificial intelligence,” that creates new content — such as emails, graphics or voiceovers.
In July, a Pentagon official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss the technology, explained the advantages of AI-driven sentiment and deception analysis.

On Friday, DCSA declined to provide additional information, including the scope of the “Modernizing Polygraph” project and the decision not to include AI-based voice screening and facial expression analysis.

In response to concerns about multimodal systems in July, the Pentagon official had said, “Any automated output is treated strictly as auxiliary data for a highly trained, certified polygraph examiner.”

In August, when the Pentagon administered a raft of polygraph exams to probe leaks alleging the Iran conflict is depleting U.S. arsenals, some observers suspected the endgame was not to find the leakers, but to crack down on disloyalty.
The expectations for AI-powered trustworthiness testing resemble the hope that U.S. national security officials held out for the polygraph about 100 years ago, other lawyers said.

“The selection of LOGIQC is a strong validation of our technological approach and the capabilities of the entire consortium.” Dr.

Sebastian Blatt, Co-Founder and CTO of planqc The project will develop a hardware-efficient, error-corrected quantum computer based on neutral ytterbium atoms, capable of performing universal logical operations on encoded qubits.
“ Germany has all the ingredients to play a leading role in quantum computing.
The QCC comes at exactly the right time to help turn Germany’s strength in quantum research into industrial leadership.” Dr.

Meaning the “color of singed beaver” in Southern East Cree , the word evokes the rich brown of the humic-substance-stained waters that were flowing into the two bays in late September 2026, as well as the role that beavers have long played in the mythology and history of the region.

When the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 captured this image on September 27, 2026, the Moose, Nottaway, and Harricanaw rivers were carrying tea-colored water across the broad mudflats of Hannah and Rupert bays and mingling with the darker blue waters of James Bay.
The mudflats, the light brown areas along the shore, are a product of the shallow, sloping bathymetry in the southernmost part of James Bay.

European traders arrived in Rupert Bay as early as the 1660s to pursue the animals as well, leading to the establishment of several trading posts along the bay’s shores and the founding of the Hudson’s Bay Company to cultivate the fur trade, especially in beaver pelts.

For instance, one Cree myth about this area, recorded by the anthropologist Alanson Skinner , tells of a giant pursuing an enormous mythical beaver down the Nottaway River until the beaver escaped into Rupert Bay.

In an early example of a managed beaver preserve in Canada, the Hudson’s Bay Company worked with local Cree people in the 1830s and again a century later to set up Charlton Island as a place to raise beavers for later trapping.

Last month, the Houthis seized Yemen's Red Sea coast and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait — a vital global shipping route — from government hands, even as Al-Alimi called for support from the international community.

evidenceRecords.text: OpenAI will watermark ChatGPT and Codex text in the EU to comply with the AI Act.
OpenAI will start adding an invisible watermark to text generated by ChatGPT and Codex in the European Union to comply with the EU AI Act, the company said Monday in a blog post.
OpenAI said the watermark will roll out over the coming weeks to eligible ChatGPT and Codex users on all plans, but only in the EU.
Developers using OpenAI’s API anywhere in the world can turn it on for select models starting today; it’s off by default.
OpenAI said it is not making text watermarking a global default at launch.
The watermark is not an actual symbol, but works by subtly shaping the model’s word choices, leaving a pattern readers can’t see, but a detector can pick up.
Because it lives in the words themselves, it travels with the text when it’s copied and pasted.
OpenAI said the watermark doesn’t identify the user, and that it saw no meaningful change in its models’ performance with it switched on.
OpenAI also published a technical report for its method, called textGrain, alongside the announcement.
Co-written with researchers from the University of Pennsylvania and Yale, it walks through an example of using a secret key to sort next-word predictions to finish the sentence.
Add hundreds of these nudges together, and the detector can spot AI-generated content using only the text and the key.
